headline: Recreation Supervisor · Army Captain
summary: Recreation Supervisor with the City of Leavenworth since 2013 and an Army Captain, leading teams as large as 60+ staff and 79 soldiers. I direct aquatics, fitness programs, and year-round community events, covering staffing, training, budgets, marketing, and facility operations. In the Army I've commanded a fuel distribution company accountable for $20 million in equipment, and I now coach and evaluate Army Reserve units in training. I bring the same planning, discipline, and standards to public service.

experience.title: Recreation Supervisor
highlights: Direct operations of the City’s indoor and outdoor pools, fitness classes, and special events.
Supervise full-time, part-time, and seasonal staff; recruit, train, schedule, and evaluate personnel.
Plan, market, and execute year-round community events, including Trunk or Treat, Holiday Markets, Breakfast with Santa, Dive-In Movies, and a Labor Day Pickleball Tournament.
Lead public relations, email and print marketing, RecDesk registration, and vendor coordination.
Monitor revenues and expenditures; process invoices and P-card reconciliations in Munis.
Oversee pool filtration, water chemistry, HVAC, and equipment to meet health and safety standards.
Red Cross Lifeguard and WSI Instructor Trainer; certify staff in Lifeguarding, First Aid, and CPR.

experience.title: Team XO, Observer Coach/Trainer (OC/T), Captain
highlights: Second-in-command of an OC/T team that coaches and trains Army Reserve units in collective training.
Lead After Action Reviews with unit leaders, assessing performance against Army doctrine and standards.
Coordinate team personnel, logistics, scheduling, and administrative requirements for exercise execution.
Mentor company-level leaders on sustainment operations, mission planning, and troop leading procedures.

experience.title: Company Commander, Captain
highlights: Led 79 soldiers across 4 platoons in a company responsible for transporting and distributing 1.5 million gallons of fuel.
Accountable for $20 million in unit equipment.
Planned and executed missions for current and future fiscal years, up to 3 years out.
Responsible for training and discipline within the unit, leading by example.
Made critical decisions that impacted higher and lower echelons.
Graduated from the Army Logistics University and completed the Quartermaster Basic Officer Leadership Course.
Oversaw 6 full-time staff leading personnel, training, operations, maintenance, and supply.

experience.title: Aquatic Manager
highlights: Served as Lifeguard, Head Lifeguard, Lifeguard Assistant Manager, Swim Instructor, Lifeguard Instructor, Water Safety Instructor Trainer, and lead recruiter.
Oversaw more than 60 staff, including lifeguards, head lifeguards, assistant managers, security, and cashiers.
Built the weekly staff schedule and delivered staff performance reviews.
Maintained pool records, filtration systems, and water chemistry through regular testing, recording, and adjustment to meet standards; monitored the HVAC system.
Recruited, trained to Red Cross standards, and hired more than 50 lifeguards.
Oversaw the City of Leavenworth’s Red Cross Learn-to-Swim program, which served an estimated 200+ children.
Coordinated with HR to deliver yearly sexual harassment training to all aquatic personnel.
Coordinated with the Police Department to conduct a yearly active shooter drill for all aquatic personnel.

experience.title: Executive Officer, First Lieutenant
highlights: Planned and executed missions for current and future fiscal years, up to 3 years out.
Managed the unit’s administration, maintenance, logistics, supply, and personnel for 79 soldiers and 103 vehicles.
Coordinated 6 full-time staff leading the personnel, training, operations, maintenance, and supply departments.
Served as primary advisor to the Company Commander on training, readiness, and day-to-day operations.
